A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SFT/RFT continual post-training study and RIF-RFT algorithm. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original continual-training experiments, general-capability evaluations, ablations, model-scale and task-order tests, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and adds difficulty-based learning curves, a random-matched filtering comparison, and split-wise POPE results.

M1.justification: The SFT/RFT objectives, reward construction and RIF-RFT procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 still filters instances using mean rollout reward above a threshold before standard RFT, with default threshold zero. Its relocation and revised motivation do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: The seven multimodal datasets, GSM8K/USMLE and general benchmarks are retained. v6 explicitly evaluates random, popular and adversarial POPE splits, but v4 does not identify the splits underlying its POPE scores. Whether this expands test-scenario coverage or further analyzes existing coverage is unresolved.

E2.justification: v6 adds GRPO trained on a random subset matched to RIF-RFT's retained dataset size as a comparator in Table 12. The other comparators, including SFT with 25% experience replay, were already evaluated in v4.

E3.justification: New protocols compare equal-sized easy, hard and mixed sample groups, match the random-subsampling control to the filtered sample count on PathVQA-to-sCLEVR, and evaluate POPE splits using Qwen3-VL-8B. The original training hyperparameters, metrics and retained experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The mechanism investigation gains an empirical difficulty-based learning-dynamics experiment replacing the schematic Figure 4. New Appendix B.3 tests whether filtering helps beyond reducing data volume, and B.4 examines hallucination by POPE split. These substantially expand the central mechanism and control analyses; existing ablations and robustness tests remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly states that results are single-run and recommends verification with multiple random seeds. v4 provides no comparable overall run-count disclosure. This does not establish a change in runs performed; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All eleven v4 tables retain their entries after matching relocations and renumbering. Targeted additions include learning curves, RIF-RFT versus random-matched average scores of 45.40 versus 42.58 in Table 12, and Qwen3-VL-8B POPE results in Table 13, including adversarial scores of 86.5 for Base, 80.9 for SFT and 87.4 for GRPO.

T1.justification: v6 removes Definition 5.1's Fisher-based forgetting risk, Proposition 5.2's reward-variance relationship, and Appendix B's assumptions, lemma and proof. Section 5.2 instead presents the policy-gradient expression and an explicitly empirical explanation, without a replacement theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list replace the theoretical reward-variance regularization contribution with empirical evidence for selective learning within model competence. They also recast RIF-RFT's contribution around training efficiency. The central claim that RFT preserves task-specific and general capabilities remains.

C2.justification: The main mechanistic interpretation shifts from variance-scaled protection to selective informative updates. v6 expands the existing filtering tradeoff by explicitly acknowledging worse accuracy and forgetting than full-data GRPO and discussing plasticity. New limitations acknowledge the unproven mechanism, missing direct interference measurements, single-run evidence and limited CPT comparisons.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds an approximate 150 GPU-hours per-sequence compute estimate, whose units are not reconciled with the retained Table 10 reporting 153.8 wall-clock hours on eight H800 GPUs. Core implementation settings, prompt templates, filtering threshold and code destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix C/Table 14 substantially expand positioning against RL's Razor and Retaining by Doing, alongside the previously discussed Zhang et al. study. v6 contrasts its sequential multimodal setting and gradient-based explanation with implicit-KL, on-policy and reasoning-data accounts.

P1.justification: v6 rewrites the abstract, contributions, mechanism discussion and conclusion. It promotes several former Appendix D analyses into Section 4.2, moves the algorithm into the main text, reorganizes the appendices, and replaces the previous ethics/reproducibility end matter with acknowledgements and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive redistribution of existing figures and tables. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, Figure 4 changes from a conceptual diagram to learning curves, and Tables 12–14 are added.

improvement.justification: The random-matched control addresses a missing test of filtering versus data-volume reduction, while the POPE diagnostics and clearer discussion of performance costs strengthen the paper. v6 also more candidly acknowledges that its mechanism remains unproven. Gains are limited: the core results are unchanged, the formal argument is removed rather than repaired, and the single-run learning curves do not directly establish reduced cross-task interference.
